subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should memory status truth come from the live gateway runtime, a passive plugin-owned local status API, or the current `not checked`/`--all` split?
rationale: Current source can support more than one plausible repair, and the repo policy treats plugin runtime loading, fallback behavior, and operator diagnostics as compatibility-sensitive surfaces that need maintainer intent before another fix PR.

options.title: Use live gateway truth for status
options.body: Make `status --deep` prefer the running gateway's memory runtime/provider health and keep local plugin materialization out of normal diagnostic output.

options.title: Define passive plugin status
options.body: Add or document a plugin-owned status hook that can report memory health locally without heavy startup, and reserve it for explicit memory-reporting modes.

options.title: Keep current split
options.body: Accept fast/deep status as `not checked` for memory and steer users to `status --all` or `memory status --deep` for heavier memory diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Use live gateway truth for status
recommendation.body: Make `status --deep` prefer the running gateway's memory runtime/provider health and keep local plugin materialization out of normal diagnostic output.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans core status UX, plugin runtime boundaries, and the memory-plugin architecture introduced in the referenced history.
